question: A shipping paper calls for a package labeled POISON or POISON INHALATION HAZARD. According to the AR CDL manual, where must you NEVER load this package?
choice_a: On the trailer's rear axle area
choice_b: In a side compartment separate from other freight
choice_c: In the driver's cab or sleeper, or with food material for human or animal consumption
choice_d: In a refrigerated section of the trailer
explanation: The manual states you must never load a package labeled POISON or POISON INHALATION HAZARD in the driver's cab or sleeper, or with food material for human or animal consumption.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 9 - Hazardous Material, p. 9-12

question: Per Figure 9.9 in the manual's mixed-loads rules, what restriction applies to nitric acid (Class 8) when loaded with other materials in the same vehicle?
choice_a: It must not be loaded above any other material
choice_b: It may never be transported with any other hazardous material
choice_c: It must be loaded in the front of the trailer only
choice_d: It must be loaded on top of all other cargo
explanation: Figure 9.9 lists nitric acid (Class 8) as incompatible with other materials unless the nitric acid is not loaded above any other material.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 9 - Hazardous Material, p. 9-12

question: What color and size must the identification numbers be on portable tanks, cargo tanks, and other bulk packaging carrying hazardous materials?
choice_a: Red 50 mm (2 inch) numbers on a yellow background
choice_b: White 150 mm (6 inch) numbers on a black background
choice_c: Blue 75 mm (3 inch) numbers on a green background
choice_d: Black 100 mm (3.9 inch) numbers on orange panels, placards, or a white diamond-shaped background
explanation: The manual requires black 100 mm (3.9 inch) identification numbers on orange panels, placards, or a white, diamond-shaped background if no placards are required.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 9 - Hazardous Material, p. 9-12 to 9-13

question: On a portable tank with a capacity of more than 1,000 gallons, how tall must the letters of the shipping name be on the two opposing sides?
choice_a: At least six inches tall
choice_b: At least four inches tall
choice_c: At least two inches tall
choice_d: At least one inch tall
explanation: The manual states the shipping name letters must be at least two inches tall on portable tanks with capacities of more than 1,000 gallons, and one inch tall on tanks with capacities of less than 1,000 gallons.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 9 - Hazardous Material, p. 9-13

question: For a portable tank or other bulk packaging holding 1,000 gallons or more, where must the identification number appear?
choice_a: Only on the rear of the tank
choice_b: Only on the driver's side
choice_c: On each side and each end of the tank
choice_d: Only on top of the tank
explanation: The manual requires the identification number to appear on each side and each end of a portable tank or other bulk packaging that holds 1,000 gallons or more.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 9 - Hazardous Material, p. 9-12 to 9-13

question: While a cargo tank is being loaded or unloaded, the qualified person watching the process must stay within how many feet of the tank?
choice_a: 100 feet
choice_b: 10 feet
choice_c: 25 feet
choice_d: 50 feet
explanation: The person watching the loading or unloading of a cargo tank must be within 25 feet of the tank, along with being alert and knowing the applicable emergency procedures.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 9 - Hazardous Material, p. 9-13

question: Before moving a cargo tank of hazardous materials, what must you do regardless of how small the amount in the tank is?
choice_a: Empty the tank completely
choice_b: Remove all placards
choice_c: Close all manholes and valves
choice_d: Fill the tank completely
explanation: The manual states you must close all manholes and valves before moving a tank of hazardous materials, no matter how small the amount, to prevent leaks; moving a cargo tank with open valves or covers is illegal unless it is empty per 49 CFR 173.29.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 9 - Hazardous Material, p. 9-13

question: Before loading or unloading a flammable liquid into a cargo tank, what should you do with the vehicle's engine?
choice_a: Rev it to clear the fuel lines
choice_b: Turn it off, running it only if needed to operate a pump
choice_c: Turn it off and disconnect the battery
choice_d: Leave it running at idle the entire time
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to turn off the engine before loading or unloading flammable liquids, only running the engine if needed to operate a pump, and to ground the cargo tank before opening the filling hole.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 9 - Hazardous Material, p. 9-13

question: When must the liquid discharge valves on a compressed gas tank be closed?
choice_a: Only while the vehicle is parked
choice_b: Except when loading and unloading
choice_c: Only when the engine is running
choice_d: Only during loading, never during unloading
explanation: The manual states to keep liquid discharge valves on a compressed gas tank closed except when loading and unloading.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 9 - Hazardous Material, p. 9-14

question: After unhooking loading/unloading connections from a compressed gas cargo tank, what must you do to trailers and semi-trailers once they are uncoupled from the power unit?
choice_a: Always chock them to prevent motion
choice_b: Disconnect the placards
choice_c: Leave the parking brake off
choice_d: Open all valves fully
explanation: The manual directs drivers to unhook all loading/unloading connections before coupling, uncoupling, or moving a cargo tank, and to always chock trailers and semi-trailers to prevent motion when uncoupled from the power unit.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 9 - Hazardous Material, p. 9-14

question: Except for short periods needed for vehicle operation necessities, how close may you park a vehicle carrying Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives to a bridge, tunnel, building, place where people gather, or an open fire?
choice_a: No closer than 50 feet
choice_b: No closer than 300 feet
choice_c: No closer than 100 feet
choice_d: No closer than 500 feet
explanation: The manual states that except for short periods needed for vehicle operation necessities, you must not park within 300 feet of a bridge, tunnel, building, a place where people gather, or an open fire when carrying Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 9 - Hazardous Material, p. 9-14

question: If you are not hauling Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives, when may you park a placarded vehicle within five feet of the traveled part of the road?
choice_a: Any time it is convenient
choice_b: Only if your work requires it, and only briefly, with someone watching the vehicle
choice_c: Only at night with hazard lights on
choice_d: Never, under any circumstance
explanation: The manual permits parking a placarded vehicle not laden with explosives within five feet of the traveled road only if your work requires it and only briefly, with someone always watching the vehicle.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 9 - Hazardous Material, p. 9-14

question: A person attending a placarded parked vehicle who is not inside it must stay within how many feet and have the vehicle in clear view?
choice_a: 100 feet
choice_b: 50 feet
choice_c: 200 feet
choice_d: 25 feet
explanation: The manual requires the attendant to be in the vehicle, awake, and not in the sleeper berth, or within 100 feet of the vehicle with it in clear view.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 9 - Hazardous Material, p. 9-14 to 9-15

question: What is a "safe haven" as described in the AR CDL manual's hazardous materials parking rules?
choice_a: An approved place, usually designated by local authorities, for parking unattended vehicles loaded with explosives
choice_b: Any rest area along the interstate
choice_c: A shipper's loading dock with security cameras
choice_d: A fire station willing to store hazardous cargo
explanation: The manual defines a safe haven as an approved place for parking unattended vehicles loaded with explosives, with designation usually made by local authorities.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 9 - Hazardous Material, p. 9-14

question: What must you use instead of flares or fuses as stopped-vehicle warning signals around a tank of flammable liquid or gas, or a vehicle loaded with Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives?
choice_a: Reflective triangles or red electric lights
choice_b: Colored smoke signals
choice_c: Handheld road signs
choice_d: A second set of headlights
explanation: The manual states you must never use burning signals such as flares or fuses around certain hazmat loads; instead use reflective triangles or red electric lights.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 9 - Hazardous Material, p. 9-14

question: If you are transporting Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives, what must you have with you and follow while driving?
choice_a: A verbal agreement with dispatch only
choice_b: A GPS tracking device only
choice_c: No special route requirement applies
choice_d: A written route plan
explanation: The manual requires drivers transporting Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives to have a written route plan and follow it; carriers normally prepare this plan in advance and give the driver a copy.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 9 - Hazardous Material, p. 9-14 to 9-15

question: How close may you smoke or carry a lit cigarette, cigar, or pipe near a placarded cargo tank used for Class 3 (flammable liquids) or Division 2.1 (gases)?
choice_a: You may not smoke within 50 feet of it
choice_b: Smoking is allowed as long as the tank is empty
choice_c: You may not smoke within 25 feet of it
choice_d: You may not smoke within 10 feet of it
explanation: The manual prohibits smoking or carrying a lit cigarette, cigar, or pipe within 25 feet of a placarded cargo tank used for Class 3 flammable liquids or Division 2.1 gases.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 9 - Hazardous Material, p. 9-15

question: What must you do before fueling a motor vehicle that contains hazardous materials?
choice_a: Turn off the engine, with someone always at the nozzle controlling fuel flow
choice_b: Leave the engine running to power the fuel pump
choice_c: Remove all placards from the vehicle
choice_d: Disconnect the trailer from the tractor
explanation: The manual requires drivers to turn off the engine before fueling a vehicle containing hazardous materials, with someone always at the nozzle controlling fuel flow.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 9 - Hazardous Material, p. 9-15

question: What minimum fire extinguisher rating must the power unit of a placarded vehicle carry?
choice_a: UL rating of 10 B:C or more
choice_b: No specific rating is required
choice_c: UL rating of 20 A:B or more
choice_d: UL rating of 5 B:C or more
explanation: The manual states the power unit of placarded vehicles must have a fire extinguisher with a UL rating of 10 B:C or more.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 9 - Hazardous Material, p. 9-15

question: According to the manual, when must you examine each tire on a hazmat-placarded motor vehicle?
choice_a: Only before crossing a state line
choice_b: At the beginning of each trip and each time the vehicle is parked
choice_c: Only when the tire looks visibly damaged
choice_d: Only once per week
explanation: The manual requires drivers to examine each tire at the beginning of each trip and each time the vehicle is parked, using a tire pressure gauge to check inflation.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 9 - Hazardous Material, p. 9-15

question: When you are behind the wheel of a placarded vehicle, where must the shipping papers be kept?
choice_a: In the trailer with the cargo
choice_b: Locked in the glove compartment
choice_c: In the sleeper berth
choice_d: Within your reach with your seat belt on, or in a pouch on the driver's door
explanation: The manual states that when behind the wheel, shipping papers must be kept within your reach (with your seat belt on) or in a pouch on the driver's door so they are easily seen by anyone entering the cab.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 9 - Hazardous Material, p. 9-15

question: What special equipment must a driver transporting chlorine in a cargo tank have in the vehicle?
choice_a: A spare cargo tank
choice_b: An approved gas mask and an emergency kit for controlling dome cover plate fitting leaks
choice_c: A hazmat suit and a portable shower
choice_d: A CB radio and extra fuel
explanation: The manual requires a driver transporting chlorine in cargo tanks to have an approved gas mask in the vehicle, plus an emergency kit for controlling leaks in dome cover plate fittings on the cargo tank.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 9 - Hazardous Material, p. 9-15 to 9-16

question: A placarded vehicle, or one carrying any amount of chlorine, must stop how far before the nearest rail at a railroad crossing?
choice_a: 15 to 50 feet
choice_b: 100 to 200 feet
choice_c: 5 to 10 feet
choice_d: 50 to 100 feet
explanation: The manual requires a placarded vehicle, or one carrying any amount of chlorine or cargo tanks used for hazardous materials, to stop 15 to 50 feet before the nearest rail at a railroad crossing.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 9 - Hazardous Material, p. 9-16

question: How is the Emergency Response Guidebook (ERG) organized so emergency personnel can find information quickly?
choice_a: Alphabetically by carrier name
choice_b: Indexed by proper shipping name and hazardous materials identification number
choice_c: By state of origin
choice_d: By vehicle type
explanation: The manual explains the ERG is indexed by proper shipping name and hazardous materials identification number, which is why the shipping paper's name, ID number, label, and placards must be correct.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 9 - Hazardous Material, p. 9-16

question: At the scene of a crash involving hazardous materials, what does the manual say about limiting the spread of material?
choice_a: Limit the spread of material, but only if you can safely do so
choice_b: Move all cargo away from the crash site immediately
choice_c: Always physically contain the spill by hand
choice_d: Ignore the spill and wait for police
explanation: The manual's crash/incident checklist directs drivers to limit the spread of material only if they can safely do so, along with keeping people away and communicating the danger to emergency responders.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 9 - Hazardous Material, p. 9-16

question: Before opening trailer doors during a suspected cargo fire, what does the manual say you should do?
choice_a: Break a window in the trailer instead
choice_b: Feel the doors to see if they are hot; if hot, do not open them, since air may make the fire flare up
choice_c: Spray water on the doors from a hose
choice_d: Open them immediately to let smoke escape
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to feel trailer doors before opening them; if they are hot, there may be a cargo fire, and opening the doors lets in air that can make the fire flare up, whereas fires without air often only smolder until firefighters arrive.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 9 - Hazardous Material, p. 9-17

question: If Class 8 corrosive materials spill or leak during transportation, what should be done to vehicle parts exposed to the corrosive liquid?
choice_a: Cover them with sand and leave them
choice_b: Wipe them with a dry cloth only
choice_c: Thoroughly wash them with water
choice_d: Apply a neutralizing acid
explanation: The manual states that parts of the vehicle exposed to a corrosive liquid must be thoroughly washed with water, and the interior should be washed out as soon as possible after unloading before reloading.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 9 - Hazardous Material, p. 9-17

question: Under the AR CDL manual, which of these is one of the conditions requiring you or your employer to phone the National Response Center after a hazardous materials incident?
choice_a: Any placard becomes damaged or illegible
choice_b: Estimated property damage exceeds $5,000
choice_c: Estimated property damage exceeds $50,000
choice_d: The delay causes the shipment to be more than one hour late
explanation: The manual lists several triggers for required notification, including a death, an injury requiring hospitalization, estimated property damage exceeding $50,000, and evacuation of the general public for more than one hour.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 9 - Hazardous Material, p. 9-18
